source_documents.title: Facile J-aggregating molecular scaffolds for chromatically tunable latent fingerprint imaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: This unique fluo rescence system is rare and achieves high quantum yields due to stable J-aggregation, driven by the molecule's intrinsic D-A-D structure and excellent planarity, as confirmed by single crystal diffraction analysis.
reference_evidence_units.subject: SQ-M1, SQ-O3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bright solid-state emission attributed to J-aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Evidence is the crystal packing; no aggregate exciton spectroscopy (e.g. band narrowing vs monomer).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Further investigation using glycerol/DMF mixtures to restrict molecular motion showed that SQ-M1, SQ-M2, SQ-O3, and SQ-O4 still maintained their non-emissive characteristics (Fig. 2b–c, and Fig. S3).
reference_evidence_units.subject: SQ-M1-SQ-O4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Restricting motion by viscosity does not turn on emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This contrasts with typical aggregation-induced emission behavior [46–51], suggesting that a different fluorescence mechanism may be involved in the solid-state emission, as their pristine microcrystals exhibit bright emission [52].

reference_evidence_units.limitations: Crystal grown from TFA; PXRD after TFA loss matches the product.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Bright crystalline emission attributed to J-aggregated slip stacks (solution and DMF/water are non-emissive). Evidence is structural (crystal packing) plus loss of emission on milling; no exciton spectroscopy.
